page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the N1 machine family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon processor cores running at 2.3 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 30 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. The underlying x86_64 architecture includes support for Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX), AES cryptography, and FMA instructions, though it lacks AVX-512 capabilities. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or bundled GPUs, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate that the n1-standard-8 delivers modest processing capabilities. In single-core and multi-core CPU tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, performance is generally positioned in the weak to poor categories, reflecting the older CPU architecture and moderate clock speed. Memory performance is mixed; while small-block cached read bandwidth is relatively low, large-block uncached read and write operations achieve average tier speeds of 45.37 GB/sec and 34.65 GB/sec respectively. Computational tasks like software compilation and text processing show lower efficiency, though ray tracing benchmarks and small-model LLM text generation manage to reach average performance levels.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-standard-8 offers a balanced resource allocation for legacy workloads that do not require high-performance computing or modern instruction sets like AVX-512. Since it lacks local storage and high-speed processing capabilities, it is best suited for general-purpose workloads such as moderate web serving, basic database operations, and lightweight background tasks. It serves as a stable, entry-level option for applications requiring dedicated vCPUs without the premium cost of newer generation hardware.
